A2 Key
Speaking test video: examiner feedback
Part 1
Debora  Inma
Debora gives a mixture of short and long
answers.
She gives some extended answers, for
example when responding to the question,
What do you like doing outdoors in your
area?  However, the details she gives are
general examples of what people can do,
Well, … you can go for hiking, trekking and
you can visit many places, it’s really nice,
and if you like you can go to visit the beach,
you can go surfing, snorkel …  , rather than
a personal response about what she likes
doing.
Debora’s language is mostly accurate, and
she uses an appropriate range of vocabulary.
Her pronunciation is clear, with minimal
examples of weaker control of sounds
(i.e.  mountain ;  visit ).
Inma gives clear, extended answers to all the
questions she is asked, right from the start of
the test.
She connects her ideas effectively, using
linking words,  because, but,  and referencing,
close to mine.
Inma’s language is generally accurate,
although she needs to be careful with
continuous tenses,  I’m always using simple
clothes … I’m always wearing black things.
Her pronunciation is usually clear, although
she sometimes drifts off at the end of
sentences, which makes some words more
difficult to hear.
Tips for Part 1
•  Practise talking about yourself, your interests and where you come from.
•  Listen carefully to the examiner’s question so that you give the correct information.
•  Think of ways to develop your answer, such as by giving reasons or examples to support
what you say.
•  The examiner has to stick to strict timing, so don’t worry if he or she has to interrupt you
while you are talking.

2
Part 2
Debora  Inma
Debora gets the conversation started well by
speaking directly to her partner,  OK, Inma … ,
and then asking her a question,  What type
of food do you like?  Later on, she keeps
the conversation going by asking another
question,  Inma, what do you think about the
fast food?
Asking the examiner to repeat a question
–  Sorry, can you repeat?  – is appropriate,
and Debora answers most of his questions
effectively. She usually gives extended
answers,  For me, I prefer a large meal
because I don’t know when I am going to
have time for eat again , but at other times
her sentences are short, with limited linking,
I don’t like too much fruit. I don’t like too
much vegetables.
Although Debora gives a full response to
the question  Do you prefer eating inside or
outside? , she misunderstands what she is
being asked and talks about eating out (i.e. at
a restaurant), in contrast to eating at home.
Debora uses an appropriate range of
vocabulary and structures, although there are
some problems with word order,  I don’t like
too much fruit .
Her pronunciation is clear, and she makes
some use of sentence stress to express her
opinions effectively.
Inma responds naturally to Debora’s
questions and uses appropriate strategies
to help her organise her thoughts,  Well … ,
But, … .  She then develops the conversation
by asking Debora for her opinion,  What do
you think about fruit and vegetables?
Inma usually checks she has understood
the question before giving an answer. She
usually answers the examiner’s questions
effectively, giving more than just simple
answers,  Yes, of course I think so; Well, I
don’t have too much time for lunch so I think
I prefer to have just a snack.
For the question  Do you prefer eating inside
or outside?,  Inma tries to check she has
understood,  If I prefer to eat at home or …?,
but does not change her response when the
examiner repeats the correct question ( Inside
or outside ), so she talks about eating at home
compared with eating out.
Inma makes good use of linking and
referencing to organise her ideas,  I don’t like
too much the desserts, to be honest, because
they are just too sweet and I don’t like the
really really sweet things … my favourite one
could be fruit or also vegetables.
She also uses a good range of structures
(i.e. language of speculation  my favourite one
could be fruit ) and vocabulary (i.e.  a proper
meal; speciality )
Her pronunciation is clear, but individual
sounds and stress for some words lack
control, e.g.  favourite,  vegetables  and
chocolate .

3 A2 Key Speaking test video: examiner feedback
Tips for Part 2
•  Listen carefully to the questions you are asked, so that you give the correct information.
•  It’s fine to ask the examiner to repeat a question or to check if you have understood the
question correctly. This also gives you thinking time.
•  Remember that the beginning of this part of the test is a conversation between you and
your partner. Practise asking questions and giving your opinion.
•  Whenever you are speaking, imagine the examiner or your partner has asked you  Why?  –
give them this information without having to be asked.

4
Overall
Debora  Inma
Grammar and Vocabulary
Debora shows control of simple grammatical
forms and uses and appropriate range of
vocabulary to answer all the questions.
Pronunciation
Debora’s pronunciation is clear, and she
demonstrates control of sounds at word and
sentence level.
Interactive Communication
Debora initiates and maintains simple
exchanges and does not require any
prompting or support. Most of her answers
are extended, although she could use more
connecting words to join her ideas in longer
sentences.
Global Achievement
Debora handles communication effectively.
She is able to produce longer utterances and
some more complex language, particularly in
the second part of the test.
Grammar and Vocabulary
Inma shows a good range of simple and
some more complex grammatical forms
and she uses a good range of appropriate
vocabulary.
Pronunciation
Inma’s pronunciation is generally clear,
although this is affected by some mumbling
at the end of sentences and some individual
sounds at word level.
Interactive Communication
Inma effectively maintains simple exchanges
and requires no prompting. Her responses
are extended throughout the test.
Global Achievement
Inma handles communication effectively,
producing long utterances and
demonstrating some range of language
throughout the test.
